name: arm-pour
_: THE POUR, one turn of the clock: home → over the can → down and grip → lift → traverse → over the glass → 120° of tool roll → away. Eight waypoints solved by closed-form IK from task space, not posed by hand. The tip is a roll of the TOOL, because the can is held with its own axis perpendicular to the tool axis — which is also why ../gripper's one-way indexer could do this move itself. Six-DOF bench arm, counterweighted parallelogram. 250 + 250 + 60 mm of arm and 181 mm of tool, shoulder at z 400, reaching a 66 × 123 can at r 500. J2 and J3 are COAXIAL at the shoulder: J2 swings the upper arm and J3 a crank whose push rod drives an elbow crank rigid with the forearm, so the forearm's ABSOLUTE angle is j3 and nothing about j2 reaches it. Three things follow — both big actuators sit at the shoulder, gravity splits into two independent one-DOF problems, and a counterweight on each rear extension balances both EXACTLY at every pose, because load and counterweight go as the cosine of the same angle. 2.55 + 4.07 = 6.62 kg of steel (CW1 at r 300, CW2 as two pucks at r 200) takes 80% of it, leaving 1.88 N·m at J2 against 9.4 bare. Deliberately not 100%: a perfectly balanced arm drifts anywhere when the power dies, an 80% one settles downward.

base-plate._: Bench plate: Ø182 × 12, four M8 on a Ø144 circle into the bench. The whole machine's overturning moment lands here — 73 N·m of it with the arm out and the counterweights swung — so it is bolted down, not weighted down. One extrude along +Z.

column._: Column: Ø84 over Ø60, z 12…240. Hollow because the J1 harmonic's cabling and the whole arm's CAN bus run up the middle — a cable bundle outside a rotating joint is the thing that fails first. One extrude along +Z.

joint-small._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø50 × 45: the wrist's three. They see inertia and a little friction, nothing else — the tool's weight is reacted at the wrist centre, not by these.

can._: A 330 ml can, Ø66 × 123. Reference geometry — it is the task, not the machine.

pin._: Ø12 ground dowel through a parallelogram joint. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: everything above the column, yawing with j1

turret._: J1 output plate: Ø92 × 14 on top of the column, carrying both shoulder cheeks. One extrude along +Z.

cheek._: Shoulder cheek, two off at |y| 56…68: they straddle the whole parallelogram and carry the COAXIAL J2 and J3 bores at z 400. Coaxial is the architecture — it is what puts the elbow's actuator at the shoulder and lets one counterweight per crank balance the arm exactly. `y1` is overridden per side. One extrude along -Y.

joint-large._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø80 × 70: NEMA 17 plus a 20:1 reduction, used at J2 and J3. Drawn along -Y; J1's instance is turned onto Z. The balanced J2 and J3 need 1.9 N·m against the 6.2 this delivers.

upper-arm._: Upper arm, J2 to the elbow, 250 mm, with a 300 mm rear extension carrying CW1. 60 × 20 on the centre plane. One extrude along -Y.

counterweight._: Counterweight: a plain steel cylinder Ø70 on a link's rear extension. CW1 is 2.55 kg (× 42.3 long) on the upper arm and CW2 4.07 kg (× 40.8) on the J3 cranks. Length is overridden per instance — the mass IS the tuning, and it is shimmable with washers. One extrude along -Y.

crank._: J3 crank, two off, coaxial with J2 and 80 mm long: the push rod hangs off its front end and CW2 off its 200 mm rear extension. The push rod delivers the forearm's whole gravitational moment here 1:1, which is exactly why a counterweight at this radius balances it at every angle. One extrude along -Y.

push-rod._: Push rod, two off, 250 mm — the same length as the upper arm and always parallel to it. That is the parallelogram: it makes the elbow crank parallel to the J3 crank, so the FOREARM'S ABSOLUTE ANGLE IS j3, whatever j2 does. One extrude along -Y.

elbow-crank._: Elbow crank, two off, 80 mm — the parallelogram's fourth bar, rigid with the forearm and reaching from its side face out under the push rod. One extrude along -Y.

forearm._: Forearm, elbow to the J4 roll section, 180 mm of a 250 mm reach. It carries no actuator: j3 arrives through the elbow crank from the shoulder. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: the wrist, at the forearm’s far end

wrist-housing._: J4 roll housing: a Ø54 tube on the forearm's own axis, 60 long. One extrude along +X.

assembly._: j5, the wrist pitch, about the wrist centre

wrist-yoke._: J5 yoke: carries the pitch axis at the wrist centre and hands the tool axis to J6. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: the tool roll, j6 — this is the pour

tool-flange._: Tool flange, ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6: Ø63 × 8, four M6 on a Ø50 circle, Ø31.5 pilot. The gripper's own web bolts to this — its README calls this interface out and does not draw it, so this is the half that exists. One extrude along +X.
